extracted.intended_audience: FCC program participants, service providers, contractors, subcontractors, consultants, marketing organizations, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for designating primary and lower tier participants, defining `principal`, applying disclosure obligations, transaction thresholds, and exclusion/suspension considerations across FCC programs (USF, Lifeline, ACP, E-Rate, RHC, TRS, NDBEDP). Useful for entities determining coverage, disclosures, and risk of suspension/debarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier framework (primary tier vs lower tier)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines use “tiers” to categorize program participants. Primary tier participants are those who deal directly with the agency or program administrators by submitting proposals for, or entering into, covered transactions. Lower tier participants are typically those who enter into covered transactions with a person at the next higher tier. Agencies have some discretion to designate participants as primary tier, lower tier, or neither.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A participant's placement in a tier can affect the scope of that participant's required disclosures and exposure to suspension/debarment. Tier designations should be applied program-by-program consistent with the adopted framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier participant two-prong test
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants are persons who (A) belong to specified categories (contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, or their agents or representatives for supported transactions) and (B) satisfy at least one of three criteria: (1) has a material role relating to, or significantly affecting, claims for disbursements related to the program; (2) is considered a 'principal'; or (3) the amount of the transaction involving the participant is expected to be at least $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both prongs must be met for the lower tier designation. The listed categories and three criteria are applied across the Covered Programs, with program-specific nuances noted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion to include subcontractors and suppliers as lower tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcontractors and suppliers are classified as lower tier participants rather than excluded from designation, to provide oversight and the ability to take exclusion action when justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: subcontractors and suppliers play essential roles and may be entrusted with large sums of Federal funds and thus can originate or amplify fraud. The expansion aims to allow comprehensive program oversight without imposing onerous requirements on primary tier participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction dollar threshold for lower tier designation ($25,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the criteria for lower tier status is that the amount of the transaction involving the participant is expected to be at least $25,000. The Commission finds $25,000 reasonable and declines to raise it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold aligns with the Guidelines' definition of 'covered transactions'. The Commission may consider actual or potential harm as a mitigating factor rather than raising a rigid higher dollar threshold; inflation or industry comparisons were not adopted as reasons to increase this threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rule for transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'transaction' can be cumulative and encompass more than a one-off funding request number (FRN), application, or monthly disbursement; the SDO must have discretion to aggregate smaller related FRNs, applications, or disbursements to meet the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents bad actors from dividing larger projects into smaller reimbursement requests to avoid the threshold. Examples: an 'act or pattern of behavior' across multiple applications, billing practices that misstate service dates, or non-usage by subscribers resulting in over-invoicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — High-Cost programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the High-Cost programs, the primary tier participant is the carrier receiving support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower tier participants for High-Cost follow the NPRM's three-category test (material role; principal; $25,000 transaction). No comment compelled modification; adopted as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — Lifeline and ACP (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Lifeline program and the former ACP, the primary tier participant is the service provider receiving support (service providers submit requests for payment to the USF Administrator and enroll subscribers). Beneficiaries (low-income consumers) generally are not considered primary or lower tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service providers are best situated to carry out primary tier obligations; interactions between low-income consumers and the Commission are incidental. For ACP Outreach grants, beneficiaries are primary tier participants (see the ACP Outreach entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier categories — Lifeline and ACP (special inclusion regardless of dollar value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants include parties (except the primary tier Lifeline carrier or ACP service provider) to any contract or award in which a person is reimbursed, including but not limited to those reimbursed based on number of Lifeline or ACP subscribers enrolled or providing commissions, regardless of dollar value. Also includes contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, agents, representatives, and third-party marketing organizations or their agents/representatives if they meet one of the three criteria (material role, principal, $25,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Lifeline and ACP many participants are treated as lower tier regardless of transaction dollar value because reimbursed-by-subscriber relationships can drive fraud; marketing organizations receive special scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — ACP Outreach Grant Program
rubrics_metrics.description: For the ACP Outreach Grant Program, the primary tier participants are the parties obtaining grants (consistent with Guidelines' sections cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although ACP appropriations were exhausted, misconduct in the ACP may still be a basis for suspension/debarment because many ACP participants also participate in Lifeline. Lower tier participants include subrecipients, contractors or subcontractors of grant recipients, or their agents/representatives if they meet one of the three criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — E-Rate program (applicants and selected service providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the E-Rate program, both the program applicant (school, library, or consortium) and the service provider(s) selected by the applicant (as indicated on FCC Form 471) are designated as primary tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating applicants as primary tier allows obtaining more extensive disclosures from the applicants and ensures applicants will obtain disclosures from service providers during bid selection. The service provider is a primary tier participant regardless of whether it submits invoices directly to USAC for reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier categories — E-Rate program
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants include contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, or their agents or representatives for E-Rate-supported transactions if: (1) they have a material role relating to or significantly affecting claims for disbursements related to the E-Rate program; (2) they are considered a 'principal'; or (3) the transaction amount is expected to be at least $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are adopted because such individuals/entities play important roles in E-Rate transactions and including them as lower tier participants is important for program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortia treatment and targeted exclusion approach
rubrics_metrics.description: When schools/libraries participate as a consortium, the consortium acting through its lead member is a primary tier participant, along with the member schools or libraries. In exclusion proceedings, the SDO should evaluate which particular consortium member was responsible for misconduct and direct suspension/debarment orders to those responsible rather than to all consortium members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a participant in an E-Rate transaction is excluded, other parties must promptly complete a service provider or SPIN change and terminate dealings with the excluded party unless an exception is granted under the Guidelines or supplemental rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — Rural Health Care (RHC) program
rubrics_metrics.description: In the RHC program, both the program applicant and the service provider(s) selected by the applicant (as indicated on FCC Form 462 or 466) are designated as primary tier participants. Consortium applicants act through a lead entity as primary tier along with member health care providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted for the same reasons as E-Rate: applicants and service providers can affect claims and are positioned to carry out primary tier obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier categories — RHC program
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants for RHC include contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, or their agents or representatives for RHC-supported transactions if: (1) material role affecting claims; (2) considered a principal; or (3) transaction amount expected to be at least $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted identical to E-Rate reasoning given similarity of program rules and participant overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier classification — TRS and NDBEDP
rubrics_metrics.description: For the TRS program and the NDBEDP, the service providers and certified programs receiving payments are deemed primary tier participants. For state-administered TRS, the TRS providers authorized by each state and compensated by the TRS Fund for provision of interstate TRS are primary tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiaries (individuals with hearing or speech disabilities) generally are not considered primary or lower tier participants in these programs because they do not directly submit applications to program administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier categories — TRS and NDBEDP (contractual supplier limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants include contractors, subcontractors, suppliers with whom the certified programs have a contractual relationship, consultants, or their agents or representatives for TRS- or NDBEDP-supported transactions if they (1) have a material role relating to claims; (2) are considered a principal; or (3) the transaction amount is expected to be at least $25,000. For suppliers, only those with a contractual relationship with certified programs are automatically deemed lower tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contractual-relationship limitation for suppliers is intended to ensure more effective enforcement for NDBEDP and TRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered transactions include transactions with program administrators/agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered transactions include not only transactions between a person and the Commission but also any transactions between a person and the administrators of relevant programs when those administrators are acting on behalf of, or as agents of, the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification ensures all transactions overseen by the Commission under these programs are covered whether the Commission acts directly or through its agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'principal' (OMB Guidelines baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines define 'principal' as: (a) an 'officer, director, owner, partner, principal investigator, or another person . . . with management or supervisory responsibilities;' or (b) a 'consultant or other person, whether or not employed by the participant or paid with Federal funds, who (1) is in a position to handle Federal funds; (2) is in a position to influence or control the use of those funds; or (3) occupies a technical or professional position capable of substantially influencing the development or outcome of an activity [in a transaction].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may identify specific examples of types of individuals who would be 'principals' under its nonprocurement programs and transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental definition of 'principal' adopted by Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the OMB baseline, the Commission adopts a supplemental definition with two components: (1) consultants who have a business relationship with participants in connection with a covered transaction, as well as Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations, shall be considered principals per se; and (2) any person having a critical influence on, or substantive control over, a covered transaction will be a principal even if not in an enumerated category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission focuses on the function the person performs, not title, employment, or payment source. This provides clarity and administrability so that certain professionals are treated as principals without a separate fact-finding process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per se exclusions and non-automatic categories for 'principal'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not categorically deem management agents, accountants, or attorneys as principals. It also removed investment bankers and engineers from the proposed list of automatically deemed principals. However, accountants or attorneys could be principals under the 'influence or control' prongs if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves case-by-case determination where function or influence demonstrates principal-level responsibilities rather than automatic categorization by profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment representatives classified as lower tier with limited disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment representatives of marketing organizations will be classified as lower tier participants because of their 'material role relating to, or significantly affecting, claims for disbursements related to the programs,' but such persons will not be deemed 'principals' except in extraordinary circumstances on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'enrollment representatives' has the same meaning as set forth in the Commission programs. The disclosure obligations of marketing representatives (lower tier) will be limited to those under section 180.355 of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of disclosure obligation options (section 180.300)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tier participants should be permitted to use any one of the three options to satisfy disclosure obligations provided in section 180.300 of the Guidelines; these disclosure obligation options are applicable to all participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary tier participants who follow the methods described in the Guidelines (largely adopted with minor modifications) can mitigate liability related to lower tier partners by collecting information consistent with the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception process for excluded parties when qualified entities are unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a service provider concludes there is a bona fide shortage of competent contractors, subcontractors, or suppliers to enable it to bid on a covered transaction, it can support an excluded party's request for an 'exception' under the Guidelines, allowing the excluded person to participate in future transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One basis for granting an exception is the unavailability of any other qualified entities to perform the necessary services. This mechanism addresses competitive options concerns raised by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors for exclusion proceedings (SDO discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines explicitly list mitigating factors the SDO may consider in evaluating exclusions, including '[w]hether and to what extent [the participant] planned, initiated, or carried out the wrongdoing,' '[w]hether there is a pattern or prior history of wrongdoing,' and '[o]ther factors that are appropriate to the circumstances of a particular case.' The Commission can also consider the 'actual or potential harm or impact' arising from wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating factors give the Commission flexibility to address each case on its merits and avoid imposing a strict liability standard. Evidence showing lack of causation by a consultant may preclude exclusion.
